comment: MiniDAQ's software items and their IEC 62304 safety classes (Chapter 14, architecture.md section 4). tools/check_items.py checks the classification rules and that every source file belongs to exactly one item. The hazards are preliminary, for classification only; Chapter 15's risk analysis replaces them. Severities are after risk controls outside the software (assumption: confirm with team).

hazards.situation: Coincidences are lost, duplicated or altered without being reported
hazards.harm: An image with wrong values or artifacts is read; misdiagnosis or delayed diagnosis
hazards.external_controls: Image review by a trained reader, daily quality control with a phantom, clinical correlation

hazards.situation: An acquisition fails or stops before its end
hazards.harm: The scan is repeated with a second injection (additional dose) or the diagnosis is delayed
hazards.external_controls: The operator sees the fault at once; the tracer allows a repeat within its half-life or on another day

hazards.situation: Data is recorded with wrong or unidentifiable settings
hazards.harm: Wrong corrections in reconstruction; as HZ-1
hazards.external_controls: As HZ-1; the effective configuration is shown to the operator

hazards.situation: An unauthorized party controls the acquisition
hazards.external_controls: The acquisition PC is in a controlled environment on a dedicated network (Chapter 17)

items.rationale: Types, units, geometry and CRC-32 used by every stage; a defect alters data (HZ-1).
Decodes readout words and packets and encodes list-mode files; a defect alters or loses data (HZ-1).
Moves every single between threads; a race loses or duplicates data (HZ-1), a deadlock stops the run (HZ-2).
Latency histograms only observe; alone class A. Class B because it runs in the server process with class B items and nothing segregates them: a memory error here can corrupt the pipeline.
Applies scheduling and memory locking; a wrong setting can starve a stage until the run fails (HZ-2).
Energy filter on the hot path, sinogram and count rates for quality control; a defect alters data or hides a problem (HZ-1).
Decides which singles form coincidences; a defect biases every count (HZ-1).
Orders the singles of many boards; a defect loses or misorders data (HZ-1).
Test sources linked into the server (problem report MDQ-PR-009); selected by mistake they produce invented data (HZ-3).
Reads and validates the acquisition settings; a defect applies a wrong setting (HZ-3).
Owns the run and its faults; a defect reports a failed run as complete (HZ-1) or stops a good one (HZ-2).
Accepts commands from the network; a defect stops a run (HZ-2) or lets an unauthorized party control it (HZ-4).
Receives the readout link and counts its losses; a defect loses data without reporting it (HZ-1).
Makes the data durable with its run record; a defect loses data (HZ-1) or its description (HZ-3).
Records control actions; its failure harms no one by itself (class A alone). Class B because it runs in the server process without segregation.
Wires the items and handles signals; a defect prevents or ends acquisitions (HZ-2).

Reference client in its own process. The server validates every request and owns the run, so a defect in the client can send a wrong but valid command, which the server reports back; no hazard beyond what the protocol item already controls.
Not shipped: development and verification tools, qualified as tools (Chapter 20).
